title: Operators & Expressions
summary: Arithmetic, comparison, and logical operators, and how Python evaluates expressions.

checkpoints.title: Arithmetic operators
checkpoints.content: Python has the usual `+ - * /` plus three worth knowing early: `//` (floor division, drops the remainder), `%` (modulo, the remainder itself), and `**` (exponent). `7 // 2` is `3`, `7 % 2` is `1`, and `2 ** 3` is `8`.
checkpoints.explanation: `//` and `%` always satisfy `a == (a // b) * b + (a % b)` — floor division and modulo are two halves of the same division.

hints.H0: Regular `/` always gives a float, even when it divides evenly.
hints.H1: `//` keeps only the whole-number part of the division.

checkpoints.title: Predict floor division

options.explanation: 17 divided by 5 is 3.4 — floor division drops everything after the decimal point, keeping 3.
That's what regular `/` would give you — `//` always returns a whole number here.
2 is the remainder (what `%` would give you), not the floor division result.

checkpoints.explanation: `//` rounds the division result down to the nearest whole number: 17 / 5 = 3.4, floored to 3.

hints.H0: Work out 17 / 5 first as a regular division.
hints.H1: Floor division keeps only the part before the decimal point.

checkpoints.title: Write a comparison
checkpoints.content: Write an expression that checks whether the variable `age` is at least 18.
checkpoints.explanation: `>=` means "greater than or equal to" — it reads left to right just like the math symbol.

hints.H0: "At least" means the value can equal the threshold too, not just exceed it.
hints.H1: You need a comparison operator that includes equality.

checkpoints.title: Combine conditions
checkpoints.content: `is_admin = True` and `is_banned = True`. What does `is_admin and not is_banned` evaluate to?

options.explanation: `not is_banned` is False (since is_banned is True), and `True and False` is False.
`not` flips is_banned to False first — `and` then needs both sides to be True, and this one isn't.

options.text: It raises an error because you can't negate a variable.
options.explanation: `not` works on any boolean value — there's no error here.

checkpoints.explanation: `not` applies first, flipping is_banned (True) to False; then `and` requires both sides True, so the whole expression is False.

hints.H0: Work out `not is_banned` on its own first.
hints.H1: `and` is only True when both sides are True.
hints.H2: `not is_banned` is False, so the whole expression is False.
